newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf says CS bid is pre-emptive.
newsitem.headline: Gulf says CS bid is pre-emptive.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd Chief Executive J.P Bryan said on Friday his firm's C$413-million bid for CS Resources Ltd would be richer than what potential competitors could offer.
Analysts, however, said they believed CS was worth more than the bid value.
"Based on what we know right now, we've made a bid that we think ought to pre-empt everybody," Bryan said in a phone interview.
"It's more than the net asset value advertised by the company in their annual report. It's more than the five-year trading high for the company. It's a nice multiple of cash flow," he said.
Gulf has yet to look at CS's books, he said.
Gulf Canada said earlier today it would offer CS shareholders either C$14.25 in cash, subject to a maximum of C$100 million, or 1.1539 Gulf Canada shares for each CS share.
However, CS quickly said it expected to announce a deal with another "strategic partner."
Analysts said the Gulf bid appeared to undervalue CS's assets and potential reserves, which were bolstered after a successful first-quarter drilling program.

Ihor Wasylkiw, analyst with Research Capital Corp, said he valued CS's reported reserves at C$13.56 a share using a 15-percent discount rate, and "somewhere north of C$16" using a 12 percent discount rate.

"I think there's room for upside," Wasylkiw said. "Aside from the different present value rates, the company has been very successful in its first-quarter drilling -- it has added incremental reserves, none of which are part of these numbers."
He also said CS's huge Pelican Lake, Alberta heavy oil property was a plum in the deal because only about 10 percent was developed and just half of the acreage developed so far had reserves booked.
Gulf sold CS the property in the late 1980s. Amber Energy Inc announced last week a tripling of reserves on its neighboring Pelican Lake acreage.

CS is a Calgary-based heavy oil producer known for its high-tech horizontal drilling and enhanced revovery techniques. Its main operating areas are in heavy oil-rich western Saskatchewan eastern Alberta.
"We think the company has excellent management, is one of the leaders in technology in this industry and we think it's got a good portfolio of assets," Bryan said.
Bryan said the cash portion of Gulf Canada's bid would be funded from company cash flow.
CS was trading up 3.60 to 14.90 on volume of over 935,000 shares. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
